checks.do: Whether access policies exist for the feature, since without them any user in the organization can connect to any enrolled endpoint.
Whether the destination's FQDN matches the Client Hostname Validation regular expression and, for a wildcard segment, the segment's domain as well.
Whether the destination's Client Connector meets the per-OS version floor and the machine tunnel or logged-in requirement for the direction in use.
Whether the case uses a feature the Zscaler IP-based server-to-client mode does not support.

client-to-client.statement: In addition to connecting users to private applications, Private Access supports connecting users to other Private Access-enabled devices for remote assistance or remote troubleshooting: an IT admin can initiate an RDP or Microsoft Remote Assistance (MSRA) connection to a remote end user's device, the connection is established by the Zero Trust Exchange, and client-based remote assistance allows troubleshooting on an end user's Windows, Mac or Linux device.

quotes: In addition to connecting users to private applications, Private Access (ZPA) also supports connecting users to other Private Access-enabled devices for remote assistance or remote troubleshooting.
An IT admin can initiate a Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connection or a Microsoft Remote Assistance (MSRA) connection to a remote end user's device if support is needed.
The connection is established by the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) infrastructure.
Enabling client-based remote assistance allows for troubleshooting on an end user's Windows, Mac, or Linux device.

c2c-client-versions.statement: Client-to-client needs end users' machines running Client Connector 3.9.0.169 or later for Windows, 1.4 or later for Linux, or 3.7 or later for macOS, with Windows and Linux devices having the primary DNS suffix properly configured and Client Connector run with Private Access enabled. The configuring article adds that Mac devices must be domain-joined.

quotes: Windows and Linux devices must have the primary DNS suffix properly configured, and end users' machines must be running Zscaler Client Connector versions 3.9.0.169 or later for Windows, versions 1.4 or later for Linux, or versions 3.7 or later for macOS.
An admin must run Zscaler Client Connector with Private Access enabled.
Mac devices must be domain-joined. End users' Mac machines must be running Zscaler Client Connector versions 3.7 or later.
Ensure the destination Windows device is running Zscaler Client Connector 3.9.0.169 or later.

c2c-destination-join.statement: Zscaler recommends that destination Windows devices for client-to-client be Active Directory domain-joined; it can also work with Windows or Linux hybrid-joined or Azure cloud-joined devices, in which case the organization must ensure the completeness and uniqueness of the destination FQDNs (for example, on Windows, that the DNS primary suffix field is entered and valid).

quotes: Zscaler recommends that the destination Windows devices you are using for this feature are Active Directory (AD) domain-joined.
However, client-to-client connectivity can work if you have Windows or Linux-based hybrid-joined or Azure cloud-joined devices.

In this case, it is your organization's responsibility to ensure completeness and uniqueness of the destination device's FQDNs (e.g., on a Windows machine, make sure that the DNS primary suffix field is entered and valid).

c2c-destination-connected.statement: For client-to-client, Client Connector on the destination machine must have a machine tunnel deployed, or the destination machine must be logged in to Private Access in Client Connector, which ensures the destination's connection to Private Access without the local user logging in to Windows.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector on the destination machine must have a machine tunnel deployed, or the destination machine must be logged in to Private Access in the Zscaler Client Connector.
This ensures the connection to Private Access for the destination machine without the original local user of the destination that is logging into Windows.

hostname-regex.statement: Client-to-client needs a regular expression configured for Client Hostname Validation, and the hostnames or FQDNs configured in client-to-client application segments must match it (for example testPC.example.com matches .*\.example\.com). Client Connector must be set to collect machine hostname information, and with a wildcard domain such as *.example.com in the segment plus a more specific expression, only devices matching both are enabled for remote assistance.

quotes: An admin must configure a regular expression in the Zscaler Admin Console for client-to-client connectivity to work.

When configuring application segments for client-to-client connectivity, the configured hostnames or fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) must match the regular expression used to validate a client hostname (e.g., testPC.example.com matches the regular expression .*\.example\.com).
On the endpoints, set Zscaler Client Connector to collect machine hostname information.
Include a regular expression in Client Hostname Validation that matches the hostname of the Windows device you are remotely accessing.

If you use a wildcard domain such as *.example.com in the application segment and a more specific regular expression in the hostname validation, only devices with hostnames matching both the wildcard domain and the hostname validation regular expression are enabled for remote assistance.

hostname-validation-enrollment.statement: Validating a client hostname enrolls endpoints for peer-to-peer connectivity so that they can accept incoming connections through Private Access from other clients. A regular expression of allowed hostnames is configured per tenant; it controls the endpoints to which Client Connector allows peer-to-peer connectivity, and endpoints whose FQDNs match it are enrolled.

quotes: Validating a client hostname allows you to enroll endpoints for peer-to-peer connectivity so that you can accept incoming connections through Private Access (ZPA) from other clients.
To enroll the endpoints, a regular expression of allowed hostnames is configured per tenant.
This regular expression controls the endpoints to which Zscaler Client Connector allows the peer-to-peer connectivity.
Endpoints whose FQDNs match this regular expression are enrolled.

pra-conflict.statement: Privileged Remote Access is not supported when an application configured for PRA matches a valid client hostname configured for peer-to-peer connectivity and the user's device is also configured for peer-to-peer connectivity.

quotes: If an application configured for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) matches a valid client hostname configured for peer-to-peer connectivity, and the user's device is also configured for peer-to-peer connectivity, then PRA is not supported.

validation-prerequisites.statement: Validating a client hostname needs Client Connector 3.9.0.169 or later installed on the destination machine, and endpoints or devices with valid, complete and unique FQDNs.

quotes: Ensure that the remote user has installed Zscaler Client Connector version 3.9.0.169 or later on the destination machine that they want to establish connectivity to.
Ensure that endpoints or devices have valid, complete, and unique FQDNs.

regex-example-and-segment.statement: The validating page's example enters the regular expression .*.example.com to establish a peer-to-peer connection for devices joined with matching domains such as test.example.com. For remote assistance to work, the application segment designated for peer-to-peer connectivity must match the regular expression entered.

quotes: For example, enter the regular expression .*.example.com to establish a peer-to-peer connection for devices joined with domains matching this regular expression (e.g., test.example.com).
To successfully enable remote assistance, the application segment designated for peer-to-peer connectivity must match the regular expression entered.

hidden-in-microtenant.statement: On the Defined Application Segments page, the Validate a client hostname option is hidden if a Microtenant is in use.

quotes: Validate a client hostname.
If you are using a Microtenant, this option is hidden.

c2c-client-connector-only.statement: Client-based remote assistance is available only to end users connecting to Private Access using Client Connector, and the server group step of segment configuration can be skipped to enable client-to-client remote assistance.

quotes: Client-based remote assistance is only available for end users connecting to Private Access using Zscaler Client Connector.
On the Server Groups tab, choose one of the following options to configure the server group accordingly, or select Skip if you want to enable client-to-client remote assistance.

c2c-segments.statement: A client-to-client application segment does not need a server group, because no App Connector has to be assigned. If applications and workstations share a namespace, Zscaler recommends separate application segments for client-based remote assistance and for application access, with separate FQDNs or wildcard subdomains if possible.

quotes: It is not necessary to select a server group because it is not required to have an App Connector assigned for client-to-client connectivity.

If you have the same namespace for both your applications and workstations, Zscaler recommends creating different application segments for client-based remote assistance and for application access, with separate FQDNs or wildcard subdomains if possible.

If you have the same namespace for both your applications and workstations and want to limit the remote assistance access only to the admin, Zscaler recommends creating different application segments for client-to-client connectivity and for application access.

open-without-policy.statement: If access policies have not been created or updated for client-to-client, any user in the organization can use the feature to connect to any endpoint enrolled in it, and an access policy controls who can connect to the remote users. For server-to-client the article says the same of any user when its access policies are not created or updated, and an existing policy can control which servers can connect.

quotes: If access policies haven't been created or updated for client-to-client connectivity, then any user in their organization can use this feature to connect to any endpoints enrolled in this feature within their organization.
Create or update an existing access policy to control who can connect to existing remote users.

If access policies are not created or updated for the server-to-client connection, then any user in their organization can use this feature to connect to any endpoints enrolled in this feature within their organization.
Create or update an existing policy to control which servers can connect to the existing remote users.

c2c-endpoint-firewall.statement: The destination endpoint's host-based firewall must allow access from the localhost using the interface IP address from the ports or protocols expected over client-to-client access. For RDP shadowing, Remote Desktop is enabled by an account with local administrator permissions, the File and Printer Sharing (SMB-In) and Remote Desktop - Shadow (TCP-In) rules are enabled, and the session is opened with mstsc /shadow.

quotes: The local endpoint (host-based firewall) must allow access from the localhost using the interface IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.100) from the ports or protocols that you expect to be available via client-to-client access.
Select Enable Remote Desktop. The account must have local administrator permissions.
Right-click File and Printer Sharing (SMB-In) and select Enable Rule.
Right-click Remote Desktop - Shadow (TCP-In) and select Enable Rule.
mstsc /shadow:<Session ID> /v:<Hostname or IP>

msra-invitation.statement: For Microsoft Remote Assistance the invitation file must be edited to remove the LHTICKET attribute and to replace the IP address in the RCTICKET value with the registered hostname in Private Access for client-to-client, edited by the destination or source user, or with the Zscaler IP for Zscaler IP-based server-to-client, edited by the destination user.

quotes: For Microsoft Remote Assistance (MSRA), the following changes must be made in the invitation file by either the destination user or the source user:
Remove the LHTICKET attribute.
Replace the IP address for the RCTICKET value with the registered hostname in Private Access.
For Microsoft Remote Assistance (MSRA) with Zscaler IP-based connectivity, the following changes must be made in the invitation file by the destination user:
Remove the LHTICKET attribute.
Replace the IP address for the RCTICKET value with the Zscaler IP.

verification.statement: To verify that a user's device is registered for remote assistance, the article says to confirm that the Valid Hostname field is True for the user's session in User Status Diagnostics; Client Connector also shows the device's FQDN in the Client field on its Private Access tab if the registration is successful. A successful client-to-client connection shows the Access Type Client to Client in the User Activity Log, and server-to-client shows the value Client to Client for the Access Type field in user activity diagnostics and live logs.

quotes: To verify that the user's device is registered for remote assistance, confirm that the Valid Hostname field is True for the user's session in the User Status Diagnostics.
Additionally, Zscaler Client Connector shows the device's FQDN on the Private Access tab for the Client field if the registration is successful.
After making the connection, if the client-to-client connection is enabled successfully, the log data in the User Activity Log shows the Access Type as Client to Client.
The data in the user activity diagnostics and live logs show the value Client to Client for the Access Type field.

server-to-client.statement: Server-to-client connectivity, a feature in limited availability, allows applications on internal servers to connect through Branch Connectors and Cloud Connectors to endpoints running Client Connector, using a Zscaler IP address or FQDN from servers that do not have Client Connector installed, for use cases such as remote troubleshooting and software distribution. This differs from client-to-client, where the connectivity is between two endpoints running Client Connector.

quotes: This feature is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
Enabling server-to-client connectivity allows applications on your internal servers to connect through Branch Connectors and Cloud Connectors to endpoints running Zscaler Client Connector.
This supports use cases such as remote troubleshooting and software distribution.
Server-to-client connectivity allows you to connect to an end user's machine using a Zscaler IP address or FQDN from servers that don't have Zscaler Client Connector installed.
This differs from the client-to-client approach where the connectivity is between two endpoints running Zscaler Client Connector.

s2c-flow.statement: With virtual Zscaler IP connectivity, an endpoint enrolls in peer-to-peer connectivity when validating a client hostname and Zscaler assigns it a virtual Zscaler IP address from the configured IP range; applications initiate connectivity to the client over that address on a specific port, and the Cloud or Branch Connector, based on policy criteria, intercepts the requests and forwards them to the Zscaler cloud. The same workflows can be achieved with FQDN connectivity, depending on how the tools connect with the endpoints.

quotes: A client or endpoint enrolls in peer-to-peer connectivity when validating a client hostname.
Zscaler assigns a virtual Zscaler IP address from the configured IP range (e.g., 192.168.254.0/24).
The cloud applications or on-premises applications initiate connectivity to the client over the virtual Zscaler IP address (192.168.254.0/24) on a specific port (e.g., 445).

Cloud or Branch Connector (as applicable and based on your policy criteria) intercepts these outgoing requests from the applications and forwards them to the Zscaler cloud for connectivity to the client or endpoint.
You can also achieve the virtual IP-based connectivity workflows using FQDN connectivity, depending on how your tools connect with the endpoints.
A Zscaler IP, which is a virtual IP address maintained by Zscaler, makes any end user's machine reachable via the Cloud or Branch Connectors for server-to-client connectivity.

s2c-requirements.statement: Server-to-client needs a deployed Cloud Connector or Branch Connector (the license to be confirmed with the Zscaler Account team), Client Connector 4.2 for Windows or later on the destination with Private Access enabled and a user logged in, a configured and validated client hostname, routing so that the Zscaler IP ranges traverse the connector, and application segments and access policies built with endpoint FQDNs or the virtual IP ranges or subnets assigned to Client Connector. For FQDN-based deployment Zscaler recommends conditional DNS forwarding so only the DNS requests of applications requiring server-to-client connections go to the connector.

quotes: Deploy a Zscaler Cloud Connector or Branch Connector.
Check with your Zscaler Account team to confirm your license for Cloud Connector or Branch Connector.
Ensure the destination device is running versions Zscaler Client Connector 4.2 for Windows or later.
Private Access must be enabled and turned on, with a user logged in, on the destination machine.
Configure and validate a client hostname to enroll endpoints and accept the incoming connections.
Create application segments that include the Zscaler IP of the clients for an IP-based connection, or FQDNs of the clients for a FQDN-based connection.
Update routing to ensure the Zscaler IP ranges traverse the Cloud or Branch Connector (e.g., 100.64.0.0/16 gateway = BranchConnectorGroup1).

If you are deploying Cloud or Branch Connector specifically for server-to-client connectivity through an FQDN, Zscaler recommends you configure conditional DNS forwarding so only the DNS requests from the applications requiring server-to-client connections are forwarded to the Cloud or Branch Connector.
Configure application segments and access policies in Private Access either with FQDNs of endpoints or virtual IP ranges or subnets that are assigned to Zscaler Client Connector.

s2c-server-routing.statement: For Zscaler IP-based server-to-client the servers' IP gateway is pointed to the Branch or Cloud Connector's service IP: on Windows with route add 0.0.0.0 mask 0.0.0.0 <service IP> metric 30 if 2, checked with route print, and on Linux with sudo route add default gw <service IP>, checked with route -n.

quotes: If you are using Zscaler IP-based connectivity, point the IP gateway from those servers to the Branch or Cloud Connector's service IP.
route add 0.0.0.0 mask 0.0.0.0 <Branch or Cloud Connector service IP address> metric 30 if 2
sudo route add default gw <Branch or Cloud Connector Service IP address>
For Windows devices, enter the following command and check that it is applied using the route print command:
For Linux devices, enter the following command and check that it is applied using the route -n command:

s2c-unsupported.statement: Server-to-client connectivity based on the virtual Zscaler IP does not support configuring a ZIA forwarding profile action using DTLA, Disaster Recovery, machine tunnels, Microtenants, or Client Connector support for multiple tenants when those tenants are partner tenants or the user is logged in to a partner tenant.

quotes: The following functions and features are not supported for server-to-client connectivity based on the virtual Zscaler IP:
Configuring a forwarding profile action for ZIA using DTLA
Disaster Recovery
Machine Tunnels
Microtenants
Zscaler Client Connector Support for Multiple Tenants. This limitation applies if those tenants correspond to partner tenants, or when a user is logged in to a partner tenant.

ip-assignment-purpose.statement: Client Connector IP Assignment controls the Zscaler virtual IP addresses assigned to clients during connectivity to the Zero Trust Exchange. The addresses do not appear in Client Connector's interface list but are unique within each Client Connector, and are used for server-to-client and client-to-client connectivity where applications cannot use FQDNs; for server-to-client the ranges must be non-overlapping and routed to the Branch or Cloud Connector as next hop router.

quotes: Client Connector IP Assignment controls the Zscaler virtual IP addresses assigned to clients during connectivity to the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE).
These IP addresses do not appear in the Zscaler Client Connector interface list, but are unique IP addresses within each Zscaler Client Connector.
These virtual IP addresses are used for server-to-client connectivity and client-to-client connectivity where applications cannot use FQDNs to connect.
For server-to-client connectivity, these IP address ranges must be non-overlapping and routed to the Branch Connector or Cloud Connector as the next hop router.

range-fields.statement: An IP range takes a name, a Status (Enabled by default; active IP addresses are unavailable to users after the range is disabled), and either an IP Range (selected by default; the beginning address must be less than or equal to the ending address) or an IP Subnet in CIDR notation used for server-to-client connectivity, plus a description and an IP Range Location, whose Latitude, Longitude, Country Code and Location Details fields are populated when the map marker is clicked. IPv6 ranges and subsets are not supported.

quotes: Name: Enter the name of the IP address range.
Status: Select the status of the IP address range (Enabled or Disabled). By default, this is Enabled.
Active IP addresses are unavailable to your users after you disable them.
IP Range or IP Subnet: Indicates if an IP address range or IP address subnet is used. By default, IP Range is selected.
The beginning IP address range must be less than or equal to the ending IP address range.
IP Subnet: The IP address subnet in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation used for server-to-client connectivity.
IPv6 IP address ranges and IPv6 IP address subsets are not supported.
Description: Enter the description of the IP address range.
IP Range Location: Enter the location of the IP address range.
If you click the location marker on the map, the Latitude, Longitude, Country Code, and Location Details fields are automatically populated.

non-overlapping-and-geolocation.statement: IP address ranges must be non-overlapping. Zscaler recommends that the ranges be broad enough to cover the endpoints based on geolocation criteria; otherwise the IP address from another available range is assigned.

quotes: IP address ranges must be non-overlapping.
Zscaler recommends that the IP address ranges are broad enough to cover your endpoints based on geolocation criteria. Otherwise, the IP address from another available IP address range is assigned.
IP address ranges must be non-overlapping.
Zscaler recommends that IP address ranges are broad enough to cover your endpoints based on geolocation criteria. Otherwise, the IP address from another available IP address range is assigned.

location-hint.statement: Send Location Hint to Client Connector is optional: the location hint is sent along with a Zscaler IP address to Client Connector, and a Client Connector that receives it creates a pseudo network adapter and applies the hint to the adapter's name for the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) location boundary.

quotes: Send Location Hint to Client Connector: (Optional) Select the checkbox to enter a location hint.
The location hint is sent along with a Zscaler IP address to Zscaler Client Connector if it is configured.

If Zscaler Client Connector receives the location hint, Zscaler Client Connector creates a pseudo network adapter and applies the location hint to the name of the adapter for the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) location boundary.

ip-ranges-page.statement: The IP Ranges page lists each range or subnet with its Location Details (City, State, Country), Total IPs, Used IPs and Status (Enabled or Disabled), and can copy (opening the Add IP Range window with the details duplicated), edit, delete or enable a range.

quotes: IP Range or IP Subnet: The IP address ranges or IP address subnets of the client or destination device.
Location Details: The location that is bound to the IP range in the following format: City, State, Country.
Total IPs: The total number of IP addresses in the range.
Used IPs: The total number of IP addresses currently used.
Status: The status of the IP range (Enabled or Disabled).
Copying an existing IP address range opens the Add IP Range window with duplicate details of the selected IP range.
Edit an existing IP address range.
Delete an IP address range.
Enable an existing disabled IP address range.

ip-bindings.statement: IP bindings indicate that a Zscaler IP address is bound to the client's destination device through Client Connector, and devices can be traced by the Zscaler IP addresses used for server-to-client or client-to-client connectivity. The page shows the Zscaler IP, range name and location, username, Client Connector platform, client hostname and last update; a CSV download is not possible when the records exceed one million, so Zscaler recommends filtering first.

quotes: IP bindings indicate that the Zscaler IP address is bound to the client's destination device via Zscaler Client Connector.
Trace client devices by Zscaler IP addresses used for either server-to-client or client-to-client connectivity based on IP address.
You cannot download the IP bindings as a CSV if the total number of records exceeds the maximum allowed limit of one million configured CSV records.
Zscaler recommends applying filters to reduce the CSV record count so that the number of records is below the configured limit.
Zscaler IP: The Zscaler virtual IP address of the client's destination device.
Range Name: The name of the IP address ranges that are bound to the client's destination device.
Range Location: The location of the IP address ranges that are bound to the client's destination device.
Username: The username authenticated on the IP address ranges that are bound to the client's destination device.
Platform: The operating system of Zscaler Client Connector.
Client Hostname: The FQDN for the server-to-client connection to Zscaler Client Connector.
Last Updated: The date and time the IP binding was last updated.

destination-machine-tunnel-or-login.summary: What the destination machine needs for peer-to-peer connectivity: a machine tunnel, or a machine tunnel or a login

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector on the destination machine must have a machine tunnel deployed.

positions.says: Client Connector on the destination machine must have a machine tunnel deployed.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector on the destination machine must have a machine tunnel deployed, or the destination machine must be logged in to Private Access in the Zscaler Client Connector.

positions.says: Client Connector on the destination machine must have a machine tunnel deployed, or the machine must be logged in to Private Access in Client Connector.

destination-machine-tunnel-or-login.impact: The validating page names only the machine tunnel, while the client-to-client configuring page also accepts a logged-in destination machine. Neither says that the validating page's requirement is limited to a particular direction, so a machine that is only logged in may or may not be enrolled; the configuring page states the wider condition for client-to-client.

field-mapping.title: How the console's Valid Hostname and Access Type labels map to the log fields
field-mapping.detail: The articles name a Valid Hostname field in User Status Diagnostics and an Access Type value of Client to Client in user activity diagnostics. The graph's log subjects use Client-To-Client Enrolled, FQDNRegistered, FQDNRegisteredError and ClientToClient; no captured page maps one set to the other.

hostname-regex-rules.title: The rules for the Client Hostname Validation regular expression
hostname-regex-rules.detail: The Validating a Client Hostname article now supplies enrollment by a per-tenant regular expression and one example (claims hostname-validation-enrollment and regex-example-and-segment), but gives no expression syntax rules: its example is written .*.example.com while the understanding article writes .*\.example\.com. The rules behind the FQDN regex error codes in zpa.logs.user-status are still not stated. The understanding article's advice on a wildcard segment for fine-grained access control is unclear and is not claimed.

s2c-platforms.title: Server-to-client version floors and support for macOS and Linux destinations
s2c-platforms.detail: Only Client Connector 4.2 for Windows is given as a floor for the server-to-client destination; macOS and Linux destinations and their versions are not stated.

ip-range-limits.title: IP range size and count limits, geolocation matching and binding lifetime
ip-range-limits.detail: No maximum range size or number of ranges is stated. How a client's geolocation is matched to a range's location is not stated, and neither is how long an IP binding lasts or whether an address is released at disconnect. Mapping console fields to the zpa/c2c-ip-ranges keys needs the SDK or Terraform source.
